question: Who was the first woman Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debala Mitra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Debala Mitra was the first woman Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), serving from 1981 to 1983.

• She was a distinguished archaeologist and art historian, well known for her authoritative work on Buddhist monuments and Indian iconography.

• Her celebrated book 'Buddhist Monuments' remains a standard reference in the field (भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण की पहली महिला महानिदेशक देबाला मित्रा थीं).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) was founded in 1861 by Alexander Cunningham, who became its first Director-General.

• The ASI functions under the Ministry of Culture and is the premier body for archaeological research and protection of monuments in India.

• It is governed by the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.

NOTE

• Kamala Das (Option 1): A famous Indian poet and author who wrote in English and Malayalam; not associated with the ASI.

• Anna Chandy (Option 3): The first woman judge (and later High Court judge) in India; a figure from the judiciary, not archaeology.

• Chitra Ramkrishna (Option 4): A former MD and CEO of the National Stock Exchange (NSE); associated with finance, not the ASI.

question: Who took oath as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in June 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is N. Chandrababu Naidu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• N. Chandrababu Naidu took oath as the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh in June 2024, following the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) led alliance victory in the 2024 Assembly elections.

• This marked his return to the CM post, leading an alliance including the BJP and Jana Sena Party (जून 2024 में एन. चंद्रबाबू नायडू ने आंध्र प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री के रूप में शपथ ली).

• He is the founder-leader and national president of the TDP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The TDP was founded by N. T. Rama Rao (NTR) in 1982.

• Andhra Pradesh's capital is planned as Amaravati.

• The Governor administers the oath of office to the Chief Minister under Article 164 of the Constitution.

NOTE

• Revanth Reddy (Option 1): The Chief Minister of Telangana (Indian National Congress), not Andhra Pradesh.

• Mohan Yadav (Option 3): The Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh (BJP).

• Vishnu Deo Sai (Option 4): The Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh (BJP).

question: In February 2025, who launched a policy report titled 'Expanding Quality Higher Education through States and State Public Universities'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2025, NITI Aayog released the policy report titled 'Expanding Quality Higher Education through States and State Public Universities'.

• The report focuses on strengthening State Public Universities (SPUs), which educate the vast majority of India's students, in line with the goals of NEP 2020 (नीति आयोग ने यह नीति रिपोर्ट लॉन्च की).

• It offers recommendations on funding, governance, quality, research and employability in state universities.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

• Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister of India, and it is headed operationally by a CEO and a Vice-Chairperson.

• It functions as the premier policy think tank of the Government of India.

NOTE

• Ministry of Education (Option 2): The central ministry overseeing education policy; it did not launch this particular NITI Aayog report.

• NGO Pratham (Option 3): An education NGO known for the ASER (Annual Status of Education Report), not this report.

• Azad Foundation (Option 4): An NGO working on livelihoods and empowerment of resource-poor women; unrelated to this report.

question: Which ministry launched the Swavalambini initiative in March 2025 to promote women entrepreneurship in India?
option_1: Ministry of Women and Child Development
option_4: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swavalambini initiative was launched in March 2025 by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), in collaboration with NITI Aayog.

• It was launched by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) Shri Jayant Chaudhary to promote women entrepreneurship among students, especially in ITIs and skilling institutions (कौशल विकास और उद्यमिता मंत्रालय ने स्वावलंबिनी पहल शुरू की).

• The programme provides entrepreneurship awareness, orientation and mentorship to young women.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The MSDE was created in 2014 to coordinate skill development efforts across India.

• Its flagship scheme is the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

• The ministry runs the Skill India Mission and oversees ITIs and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).

NOTE

• Ministry of Women and Child Development (Option 1): Runs schemes like Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and Mission Shakti, but did not launch Swavalambini.

• Ministry of Rural Development (Option 2): Handles rural livelihoods (e.g., MGNREGA, DAY-NRLM); not associated with this initiative.

• Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Option 3): Deals with trade and industry policy; unrelated to Swavalambini.

question:
In India, which of the following is a report published under MoSPI?
I. Periodic Labour Force Survey
II. Monthly Infrastructure Performance Review Report
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) publishes the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), which gives key employment-unemployment indicators.

• MoSPI's Infrastructure and Project Monitoring Division also brings out infrastructure and project-performance review reports, making both statements correct (पीएलएफएस और अवसंरचना प्रदर्शन समीक्षा रिपोर्ट दोनों मोएसपीआई के तहत प्रकाशित होती हैं).

• Hence both I and II are reports connected with MoSPI.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The PLFS was launched by the National Statistical Office (NSO) in 2017.

• MoSPI is responsible for computing key indicators like GDP, IIP and CPI.

• MoSPI has two wings: the National Statistical Office (NSO) and the Programme Implementation Wing.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because MoSPI publishes both the PLFS and infrastructure performance-review reports.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since the PLFS is also a MoSPI publication.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both statements are true.

question: The Sudasari Great Indian Bustard Breeding centre is in which of the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sudasari Great Indian Bustard Breeding Centre is located in Rajasthan, within the Desert National Park area near Jaisalmer.

• It is part of the conservation-breeding programme to save the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB) (सुदासरी ग्रेट इंडियन बस्टर्ड प्रजनन केंद्र राजस्थान में है).

• The Great Indian Bustard is the state bird of Rajasthan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The GIB (scientific name Ardeotis nigriceps) is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.

• The 'Project Great Indian Bustard' conservation effort is run in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII).

• Rajasthan also hosts the campaign nickname 'Godawan' for the GIB.

NOTE

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Known for the Vedanthangal and Point Calimere bird sanctuaries, not GIB breeding.

• Kerala (Option 3): Home to bird sanctuaries like Thattekad, but not associated with the GIB breeding centre.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Has GIB sightings historically but the Sudasari centre is not located here.

question: Who is the author of a travel book 'From Heaven Lake: Travels Through Sinkiang and Tibet', which won the Thomas Cook Travel Book Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikram Seth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vikram Seth authored the travel book 'From Heaven Lake: Travels Through Sinkiang and Tibet' (1983), which won the Thomas Cook Travel Book Award.

• It recounts his journey through China (Sinkiang/Xinjiang and Tibet) back to India (यह पुस्तक विक्रम सेठ ने लिखी).

• He is one of India's most acclaimed English-language writers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vikram Seth's celebrated novel 'A Suitable Boy' (1993) is one of the longest novels in English.

• His novel-in-verse 'The Golden Gate' (1986) is written entirely in sonnets.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2007.

NOTE

• Sarah Joseph (Option 1): A well-known Malayalam novelist and activist; did not write this book.

• Rohit Lal (Option 2): Not a recognised author associated with this travel book.

• Kanchana Banerjee (Option 3): A contemporary Indian fiction writer, not the author of this work.

question: The 'Vamsi', a traditional instrument of Tamil Nadu, is a _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Vamsi' (also spelt Vamshi/Venu) is a traditional flute, a wind instrument (aerophone).

• The Sanskrit word 'Vamsi' derives from 'Vamsha' meaning bamboo, from which flutes are traditionally made (वामसी एक बांसुरी है).

• It belongs to the family of bamboo flutes used in South Indian and classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Musical instruments are broadly classified into Tata (string), Sushira (wind), Avanaddha (percussion/membrane) and Ghana (solid) vadya.

• The flute is a Sushira Vadya (wind instrument).

• Pannalal Ghosh is regarded as a pioneer of the classical bamboo flute in Hindustani music.

NOTE

• Drum (Option 2): A percussion (membranophone) instrument, not a flute.

• Sarod (Option 3): A plucked stringed instrument (chordophone) used in Hindustani classical music.

• Manjira (Option 4): A pair of small metallic cymbals (idiophone), not a flute.

question: 'Swang' dance is performed in which of the following Indian state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Swang is a popular folk theatre-cum-dance form performed mainly in Uttar Pradesh (and also in Haryana).

• It combines music, dance, drama and satire, with performers enacting mythological and social themes (स्वांग नृत्य उत्तर प्रदेश में किया जाता है).

• The word 'Swang' literally means imitation or impersonation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Two major styles of Swang are the Rohtak (Haryanvi) and Hathras (Uttar Pradesh) schools.

• Other folk forms of Uttar Pradesh include Nautanki, Raslila and Charkula.

• Kathak, a classical dance, also has strong roots in Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow gharana).

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Dekhni, Fugdi and Ghode Modni, not Swang.

• Kerala (Option 2): Famous for Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam.

• Karnataka (Option 3): Known for Yakshagana and the classical dance Bharatanatyam traditions.

question:
In the context of Indian satellite, the INSAT is used for which of the following purpose?
I. Television broadcasting
II. Weather Forecasting
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The INSAT (Indian National Satellite System) is a series of multipurpose geostationary satellites.

• It is used for telecommunications, television broadcasting, meteorology (weather forecasting), search and rescue, and disaster warning (इनसैट का उपयोग टेलीविजन प्रसारण और मौसम पूर्वानुमान दोनों के लिए होता है).

• Hence both television broadcasting and weather forecasting are valid uses.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The INSAT system was commissioned in 1983 and is one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in the Asia-Pacific region.

• It is operated jointly by ISRO, Department of Space, Department of Telecommunications, IMD and others.

• Dedicated meteorological satellites in this family include the Kalpana-1 and INSAT-3D series.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since INSAT is also used for weather forecasting.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since INSAT is also used for television broadcasting.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as INSAT serves both purposes.

question: Newton's third law of motion states that _____.
option_1: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction
option_2: For every action, the reaction is opposite but greater in magnitude
option_3: The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the applied unbalanced force in the direction of force
option_4: An object in motion remains in motion unless acted upon by a force
solution_text:
The correct answer is For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Newton's Third Law of Motion states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

• The action and reaction forces act on two different bodies, are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction (प्रत्येक क्रिया के लिए, समान किंतु विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया होती है).

• Examples include the recoil of a gun and the propulsion of a rocket.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia): A body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

• Newton's Second Law: Force equals the rate of change of momentum (F = ma).

• These laws were published by Isaac Newton in his work 'Principia Mathematica' (1687).

NOTE

• Reaction opposite but greater in magnitude (Option 2): Incorrect, as action and reaction are always equal in magnitude.

• Rate of change of momentum proportional to force (Option 3): This describes Newton's Second Law, not the third.

• Object in motion remains in motion (Option 4): This describes Newton's First Law (inertia).

question: What is the formula for pressure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pressure = force / area.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pressure is defined as the force acting perpendicularly per unit area: Pressure = Force / Area (दाब = बल / क्षेत्रफल).

• Its SI unit is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

• For a fixed force, a smaller area produces greater pressure (e.g., a sharp knife cuts more easily).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pressure is a scalar quantity.

• Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 101,325 Pa (1 atm).

• Other units include bar, atmosphere (atm) and torr.

NOTE

• Force × area (Option 2): Incorrect; multiplying force by area does not give pressure.

• Area / force (Option 3): This is the inverse of the pressure relation, hence wrong.

• (force × force) / area (Option 4): Dimensionally incorrect and not a valid pressure formula.

question: The uncrewed Gaganyaan-G1 mission, scheduled for December 2025, will carry a female-looking half-humanoid robot to test human functions and onboard systems. What is the name of this robot?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vyommitra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vyommitra is the female-looking half-humanoid robot developed by ISRO to fly on the uncrewed Gaganyaan-G1 mission.

• It is designed to simulate human functions, monitor onboard systems and respond to the environment during the test flight (इस रोबोट का नाम व्योममित्र है).

• The name combines 'Vyoma' (space) and 'Mitra' (friend), meaning 'space friend'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Gaganyaan is India's first human spaceflight programme, led by ISRO.

• The programme aims to send Indian astronauts ('Vyomanauts'/Gagannauts) into low Earth orbit.

• The crewed mission is planned to carry astronauts for a few days in orbit and return them safely.

NOTE

• Manavi (Option 1): Not the name of ISRO's Gaganyaan humanoid robot.

• Bhumika (Option 3): Not associated with the Gaganyaan humanoid; a distractor name.

• Rakshak (Option 4): Not related to the Gaganyaan robot; used generally to mean 'protector'.

question: In August 2025, which organisation received an order worth Rs. 62000 crores for 97 LCA Mk1A fighter jets from the Indian government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is HAL.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2025, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) received an order worth about Rs. 62,000 crore for 97 LCA Tejas Mk1A fighter jets from the Government of India.

• The LCA Tejas is an indigenous single-engine, multirole light combat aircraft (यह ऑर्डर एच.ए.एल. को प्राप्त हुआ).

• This order strengthens India's push for self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat) in defence manufacturing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• HAL is a public-sector aerospace and defence company headquartered in Bengaluru, established in 1940.

• The LCA Tejas was designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) and built by HAL.

• HAL also manufactures helicopters like the Dhruv (ALH) and Light Combat Helicopter (Prachand).

NOTE

• AWE India (Option 2): Not the recipient of this fighter-jet order.

• DRDO (Option 3): The Defence Research and Development Organisation designs and develops defence technology but does not manufacture and supply aircraft under such production orders.

• AVANI (Option 4): Not a defence-manufacturing organisation relevant to this order.

question: In 1722, Sawai Raja Jai Singh was given the governorship of which of the following regions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1722, Sawai Raja Jai Singh II was granted the subedari (governorship) of Agra by the Mughal emperor.

• He was the Rajput ruler of Amber and later founded the city of Jaipur in 1727 (1722 में सवाई जय सिंह को आगरा की सूबेदारी दी गई थी).

• He was a noted astronomer, administrator and city planner.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sawai Jai Singh II built the astronomical observatories called Jantar Mantar at Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura.

• He compiled the astronomical tables known as the 'Zij-i-Muhammad Shahi'.

• Jaipur, his planned capital, is famous as the 'Pink City'.

NOTE

• Bengal (Option 1): In the early 18th century Bengal was governed by nawabs such as Murshid Quli Khan, not Jai Singh.

• Awadh (Option 2): Its subedari was associated with Saadat Khan (Burhan-ul-Mulk), founder of the Awadh dynasty.

• Odisha (Option 4): Was administratively linked to Bengal under the nawabs, not to Jai Singh.

question: Which of the following tax are imposed on goods imported into and exported out of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Customs duty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Customs duty is the tax imposed on goods imported into and exported out of India.

• It is levied under the Customs Act, 1962, and administered by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) (आयातित और निर्यातित वस्तुओं पर सीमा शुल्क लगाया जाता है).

• It is an indirect tax and also serves to regulate the flow of goods across borders.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Customs duty includes Basic Customs Duty (BCD) and additional levies such as IGST on imports.

• After GST, most domestic indirect taxes were subsumed, but customs duty remains separate.

• Import duty protects domestic industries, while some export duties are used to conserve resources.

NOTE

• Excise duty (Option 1): A tax on the manufacture/production of goods within the country (now largely subsumed under GST, except items like petroleum and liquor).

• Wealth tax (Option 3): A direct tax on net wealth, abolished in India in 2015.

• Estate duty (Option 4): A tax on property inherited after death; abolished in India in 1985.

question: The target of National Logistics Policy is to improve India's Logistics performance index ranking to among top 25 countries by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2030.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Logistics Policy (NLP), launched in September 2022, targets improving India's Logistics Performance Index (LPI) ranking to among the top 25 countries by 2030.

• It also aims to reduce logistics costs in India to be comparable with global benchmarks (राष्ट्रीय लॉजिस्टिक्स नीति का लक्ष्य 2030 तक शीर्ष 25 देशों में लाना है).

• The policy seeks to make logistics efficient, seamless and technology-driven.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NLP complements the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (2021).

• The Logistics Performance Index (LPI) is published by the World Bank.

• Key elements of the NLP include the Integration of Digital System (IDS), Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) and a system improvement group.

NOTE

• 2027 (Option 1): Not the target year specified in the National Logistics Policy.

• 2040 (Option 3): Incorrect; the LPI top-25 target is set for 2030.

• 2047 (Option 4): This is the horizon for 'Viksit Bharat', not the NLP's LPI top-25 goal.

question: In which year was the Special Economic Zones (SEZs) policy was launched in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Special Economic Zones (SEZs) policy was announced in India in April 2000.

• It aimed to promote exports, attract foreign investment and generate employment by creating duty-free enclaves treated as foreign territory for trade operations (एस.ई.जेड. नीति वर्ष 2000 में शुरू की गई थी).

• It was later given a statutory basis by the SEZ Act, 2005, which came into force in 2006.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Asia's first Export Processing Zone (EPZ) was set up at Kandla (Gujarat) in 1965.

• SEZs offer benefits such as tax holidays, duty-free imports and simplified procedures.

• The SEZ policy is administered by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

NOTE

• 1998 (Option 1): Not the year the SEZ policy was announced.

• 2002 (Option 2): Incorrect; the policy predates this year.

• 1999 (Option 3): Incorrect; the SEZ policy was launched in 2000, not 1999.

question: An Indian state can be divided or its boundary altered by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parliament.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 3 of the Constitution, only the Parliament can form new states and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states.

• Such a bill can be introduced only on the recommendation of the President, and the President refers it to the concerned State Legislature for its views (which are not binding) (संसद किसी भारतीय राज्य को विभाजित या उसकी सीमा परिवर्तित कर सकती है).

• It can be passed by a simple majority and is not treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 1 describes India as a 'Union of States'.

• Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new states into the Union.

• Recent reorganisation examples include the creation of Telangana (2014) and the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir into Union Territories (2019).

NOTE

• The State Legislature (Option 1): Only expresses its (non-binding) views; it cannot itself alter state boundaries.

• President (Option 3): Recommends introduction of the bill, but cannot alter boundaries; this power lies with Parliament.

• Supreme Court (Option 4): Interprets the Constitution and settles disputes, but does not create or reorganise states.

question: Which of the following is NOT constitute the hinterland of Marmagao port?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Marmagao (Mormugao) Port is located in Goa on the west coast of India.

• Its hinterland consists of Goa, Karnataka and southern Maharashtra, from where it draws its trade (mainly iron-ore exports) (हिमाचल प्रदेश मार्मागाओ बंदरगाह का पृष्ठ प्रदेश नहीं है).

• Himachal Pradesh, a landlocked northern state, is far from the port and does NOT form its hinterland.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Marmagao Port is traditionally India's premier iron-ore exporting port.

• It lies at the mouth of the Zuari River estuary.

• A hinterland is the inland region served by a port for its imports and exports.

NOTE

• Karnataka (Option 1): A key part of Marmagao's hinterland, supplying iron ore for export.

• Goa (Option 2): The state where the port is located and its immediate hinterland.

• Southern Maharashtra (Option 3): Also forms part of the port's hinterland region.

question: What is a capital goods industry?
option_1: Industry that deals in external commercial borrowings.
option_3: Industry that process raw agricultural product.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Industry producing machines and tools.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A capital goods industry is one that produces machines, tools, equipment and plant used to manufacture other goods.

• Capital goods are not for final consumption; they are used as inputs in the production process of other goods and services (पूँजीगत वस्तु उद्योग वह है जो मशीनें और कलपुर्जे बनाता है).

• Examples include machine tools, industrial machinery and heavy equipment manufacturing.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Capital goods are also called producer goods or investment goods.

• Heavy industries like BHEL are prominent capital-goods manufacturers in India.

• In contrast, consumer goods are meant for direct final use by consumers.

NOTE

• Deals in external commercial borrowings (Option 1): This describes a financial activity, not a capital-goods industry.

• Exports food products (Option 2): This relates to the food-processing/agro-export sector, not capital goods.

• Processes raw agricultural product (Option 3): This describes an agro-based or processing industry, not a capital-goods industry.

question:
In the context of trade policy tools, which of the following is considered as tariff measure?
I. Export taxes
II. Import taxes
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A tariff is a tax or duty imposed on goods that cross international borders.

• Both export taxes (levied on goods leaving the country) and import taxes (levied on goods entering the country) are tariff measures (निर्यात कर और आयात कर दोनों प्रशुल्क उपाय हैं).

• Hence both statements I and II are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Trade policy tools are broadly divided into tariff and non-tariff measures.

• Non-tariff barriers include quotas, licensing, subsidies and standards.

• Import tariffs protect domestic industry, while export tariffs may conserve scarce resources or raise revenue.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because import taxes are also tariff measures.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because export taxes are also tariff measures.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, as both export and import taxes are tariff measures.

question: As of February 2025, Scheduled Tribe (ST) individuals comprising _____ of the total population in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.6%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Scheduled Tribes (STs) constitute about 8.6% of India's total population, as per the Census 2011 figures used as the reference.

• Scheduled Castes (SCs) in comparison form about 16.6% of the population (अनुसूचित जनजाति की संख्या भारत की कुल जनसंख्या का 8.6% है).

• STs are recognised under Article 342 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population among Indian states, while Mizoram has the highest proportion of STs.

• The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) was set up under Article 338A.

• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for ST welfare.

NOTE

• 5.5% (Option 2): An underestimate; the actual ST share is around 8.6%.

• 9.8% (Option 3): Higher than the correct figure of about 8.6%.

• 12.2% (Option 4): Too high; this does not match the ST share of India's population.

question: What is the process called when organisms acquire oxygen from outside the body to break down food sources?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Respiration.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Respiration is the process by which organisms take in oxygen and use it to break down food (glucose) to release energy (ATP).

• Aerobic respiration requires oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water as by-products (श्वसन वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें बाहर से ऑक्सीजन लेकर भोजन का विघटन होता है).

• It occurs mainly in the mitochondria, often called the 'powerhouse of the cell'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The overall equation of aerobic respiration: C6H12O6 + 6O2 → 6CO2 + 6H2O + energy.

• Anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen (e.g., in muscle cells producing lactic acid).

• Breathing (exchange of gases) is distinct from cellular respiration (energy release).

NOTE

• Digestion (Option 2): The breakdown of food into simpler absorbable substances, not the oxygen-based energy-release process.

• Photosynthesis (Option 3): The process by which green plants make food using sunlight, CO2 and water, releasing oxygen.

• Fermentation (Option 4): An anaerobic breakdown of sugars without oxygen, e.g., producing alcohol or lactic acid.

question: The 'Charaksamhita' is a treatise on which of the following subjects?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Medicine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 'Charaka Samhita' is an ancient Sanskrit treatise on medicine (Ayurveda).

• It is attributed to Charaka and is one of the foundational texts of the Indian system of medicine (चरकसंहिता आयुर्विज्ञान/चिकित्सा पर एक ग्रंथ है).

• It deals with diagnosis, treatment, diet and general principles of internal medicine.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Charaka is often called the 'Father of Indian Medicine'.

• The 'Sushruta Samhita', by Sushruta, is the classic text of ancient Indian surgery; Sushruta is called the 'Father of Surgery'.

• The three great classics of Ayurveda (Brihat-Trayi) are the Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita and Ashtanga Hridaya.

NOTE

• Astronomy (Option 2): Texts like the 'Aryabhatiya' by Aryabhata deal with astronomy, not the Charaka Samhita.

• Architecture (Option 3): Subjects like architecture are covered in Vastu Shastra and Shilpa Shastra texts.

• Mathematics (Option 4): Mathematical works include Aryabhata's and Brahmagupta's treatises, not the Charaka Samhita.
